links.outcome: Change in ESI assignment under gender-swapped counterfactual vignettes (flip rate, F/M undertriage ratio)
links.effect: All five models exceeded the pre-registered 5% flip threshold (9.9% to 43.8%); DeepSeek F/M 2.15:1 and Gemini 1.34:1 directional female undertriage.
links.quote: All five models produced flip rates above a pre-registered 5% threshold (9.9% to 43.8%).

links.outcome: Subgroup-specific bias hidden from aggregate performance in LLM triage
links.effect: DeepSeek's directional bias coexisted with a low outcome-linked calibration gap (0.013), showing group calibration can mask counterfactual non-invariance.
links.quote: DeepSeek's directional bias coexisted with a low outcome-linked calibration gap (0.013 against MIMIC-IV admission), a Chouldechova-style dissociation between within-group calibration and between-pair counterfactual invariance.

links.outcome: Effect of demographic blinding on flip rate and directional bias
links.effect: Blinding reduced Gemini's flip rate to 0.5%; age-preserving blind variant left DeepSeek with residual F/M 1.25, so effectiveness was model-dependent.
links.quote: Demographic blinding reduced Gemini's flip rate to 0.5%; an age-preserving blind variant left DeepSeek with residual F/M 1.25, implicating age as a residual channel.

links.outcome: Accuracy of ESI assignment under chain-of-thought prompting versus other prompt strategies
links.effect: Chain-of-thought prompting degraded accuracy for all five models.
links.quote: Chain-of-thought prompting degraded accuracy for all five models.

unlisted_practices: Demographic blinding of model inputs to reduce gender bias
Per-model counterfactual auditing before clinical deployment

screen.reason: The study conducts a fairness audit of LLMs on emergency department triage vignettes, specifically testing deployment mitigation practices such as demographic blinding and prompting strategies (e.g., chain-of-thought) to assess their impact on gender bias and accuracy.
